question: Should OpenClaw support a Telegram-specific presence lifecycle for existing accounts, and if so should it be opt-in rather than activated by an absent configuration block?
rationale: The branch adds a new visible channel behavior and configuration surface whose safe upgrade default and relationship to existing reactions are product-contract decisions, not a mechanical repair.

options.title: Sponsor a revised opt-in feature
options.body: Keep the PR direction, but require a refreshed implementation that authorizes first, preserves reaction ownership, wires strict config validation, and opts existing accounts in explicitly.

options.title: Adopt a narrower existing-feedback path
options.body: Decline this parallel lifecycle and improve the existing acknowledgement or typing mechanisms instead, avoiding a second Telegram reaction owner.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Close or pause the branch until maintainers choose a supported cross-channel feedback model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a revised opt-in feature
recommendation.body: Keep the PR direction, but require a refreshed implementation that authorizes first, preserves reaction ownership, wires strict config validation, and opts existing accounts in explicitly.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior proof and review-cycle involvement provides the strongest available routing signal for the Telegram behavior decision.
